sources.entry: Python: _Build Deep Learning From Scratch (reimplement PyTorch internals across 34 stages)_

summary.one_liner: A 35-stage project-based curriculum where you reimplement PyTorch's internals (autodiff, tensors, layers, optimizers, CNNs, attention, Transformers) from scratch using only NumPy, Matplotlib, and pytest.
summary.what_it_does: It is a structured course in which each stage has a README, a skeleton code.py with TODOs, and a test.py containing pytest tests, including numerical gradient checks via central differences. It starts with a scalar Value class and a reverse-mode autodiff engine modeled on Karpathy's micrograd (stages 01-05), then generalizes to an N-dimensional NumPy-backed Tensor (stage 08). Later stages build neurons, dense layers, MLPs, losses, optimizers (SGD, momentum, Adam), batching and DataLoader, regularization, dropout, BatchNorm, and Conv2D/pooling. The final stages cover attention, multi-head attention, Transformer blocks, a Vision Transformer, a PyTorch-like Module/Parameter API, and capstones on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and a Transformer language model. Reference solutions are on a separate solutions branch, which the README says is solved through stage 17 at present.
use_cases: learn how backpropagation and autodiff work by coding them
understand PyTorch internals by reimplementing them
study a from-scratch Transformer or attention implementation
work through a guided deep learning course with tests
practice gradient derivations with numerical checks
build a small PyTorch-like framework as a learning project
complete MNIST or CIFAR-10 classifier exercises from scratch
how_to_run: Repeat stage by stage in order
Optionally: git checkout solutions to compare against reference implementations (solved through stage 17)
notable: Forbids autodiff libraries (torch, tensorflow, jax, micrograd) until a concept is built by hand
Each stage ships README, skeleton code.py, and test.py with numerical gradient checks
Includes an AI tutor prompt (tutor_skill.md) that gives hints without handing over solutions
Covers scalar autodiff through Transformer, ViT, and three capstone projects in 35 stages
Reference solutions on a separate solutions branch
caveats: Estimated effort is 150-250 hours end to end
Reference solutions are only available through stage 17 at the time of the README; later stages are still being added
Skeleton-only main branch means you must write all implementations yourself
